title: The economic centre of gravity
hook: For 2,000 years, the world's economic centre has been on the move.
notes: Illustrative reconstruction after McKinsey Global Institute (2012), 'Urban world'. Positions are approximate. The centre of gravity is calculated through the Earth and then placed on the surface, which is why it sits so far north.

scenes.title: A single moving dot
scenes.text: Weight every place on Earth by its economic output and find the balance point. Drag the slider to watch it travel.

captions.1: Year 1: China and India dominate world output. The centre sits in Central Asia.
captions.1000: Year 1000: little changes for a millennium.
captions.1500: 1500: Europe begins to grow, Asia still leads.
captions.1820: 1820: the Industrial Revolution starts pulling the centre west.
captions.1870: 1870: Britain is the workshop of the world.
captions.1940: 1940: the centre crosses into the Atlantic.
captions.1950: 1950: the most westerly point. The US alone produces over a quarter of world output.
captions.2010: 2010: faster than at any time in history.

scenes.title: Back to Asia
scenes.text: For most of history, China and India produced most of the world's output. Industrialisation pulled the centre to the North Atlantic. Since 1980 it has been racing back east.
